newsitem.title: USA: Tambrands up on P&G deal rumor-mkt sources.
newsitem.headline: Tambrands up on P&G deal rumor-mkt sources.

text.p: Tambrands Inc shares climbed higher in unusually heavy trade Tuesday on speculation that the company is in talks to merge with Procter & Gamble Co, according to market sources.
Neither company was immediately available to comment on the rumors or stock activity.
During the day, Tambrands shares hit a high of 48-1/8 but eased back to 46-3/8, up 7/8, in late trading.
Meanwhile, P&G shares fell 1-1/2, or 1.5 percent, to 115-3/4, also in unusually active trade.
Options traders said investors were actively buying Tambrands call options, which stand to rise in value if the stock rallies.
They said the call buying, which had been increasing since late last week, was driven by takeover speculation.
An analyst who declined to be identified outlined several reasons P&G has stated for not seeking a transaction that would give the company a significant share of the feminine hygiene market.
"But the caveat there is this is same company that told me they would never get into cosmetics," the analyst added.
In 1991, P&G acquired from Revlon Inc the Max Factor cosmetics line. P&G also owns the Cover Girl make-up line.
The analyst added that P&G has said it is not interested in tampons because the business's global potential is limited due to cultural issues.
